identification.summary: Mandiant described UNC5337 as a suspected China-nexus espionage cluster that compromised Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances as early as January 2024, suspected of using CVE-2023-46805 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2024-21887 (command injection) [S1]. It was associated with the custom SPAWN malware ecosystem (SPAWNANT installer, SPAWNMOLE tunneler, SPAWNSNAIL backdoor, SPAWNSLOTH log tamperer) [S1]. Mandiant assessed with medium confidence that UNC5337 was UNC5221 [S3], and in its January 2025 post stated that UNC5337 had been merged into UNC5221 (attribution updated 2025-01-17) [S2].
identification.notes: UNC5337 is a retired/merged Mandiant cluster; current Mandiant tracking is under UNC5221 [S2]. Do not merge facts from other Ivanti clusters (for example UNC5325, UNC5330) into this record; one outlet's search coverage used UNC5325 for the SPAWNCHIMERA actor, which conflicts with Mandiant's naming and is unresolved [S4]. No Microsoft name is stated in the cited sources.

attribution.confidence: Mandiant labels the cluster 'suspected China-nexus' [S1][S2]. Mandiant assessed with medium confidence that UNC5337 is UNC5221 (per secondary coverage; exact date and wording not verified) [S3], then merged the two clusters in January 2025 [S2]. In January 2025 Mandiant said it lacked data to assess how many actors were exploiting CVE-2025-0282 [S3].
attribution.basis: Mandiant analysis of compromised ICS appliances and malware overlap with UNC5221 [S1][S2]. No government attribution is cited here.

targeting.notes: Mandiant's April 2024 post does not identify UNC5337 victims or sectors [S1]. Victimology for the associated UNC5221 activity is not established in the sources gathered.

capabilities.summary: Exploitation of ICS zero-days: CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 (UNC5221 exploited these before the 2024-01-10 disclosure) [S1][S2]. SPAWN family: SPAWNANT hijacks the dspkginstall process and persists SPAWNMOLE and SPAWNSNAIL; SPAWNMOLE injects into the web process, hooks accept and tunnels attacker traffic; SPAWNSNAIL injects into dsmdm and provides a limited SSH server on localhost port 8300 requiring public-key authentication; SPAWNSLOTH disables syslog forwarding while SPAWNSNAIL runs [S1]. Mandiant noted the SPAWN analysis came from an appliance compromised by UNC5221 [S1]. In the January 2025 CVE-2025-0282 campaign Mandiant reported recon of ICS version-identifying URLs, SELinux disabling, syslog blocking, web shells (PHASEJAM), fake upgrade progress to block upgrades, integrity-checker manifest tampering, DRYHOOK credential harvesting, LDAP and SMB/RDP lateral movement and log cleaning, and said the SPAWN ecosystem was attributed to UNC5337 (now UNC5221) while it could not tie all CVE-2025-0282 activity to one actor [S2][S3]. CISA later analyzed RESURGE, a SPAWNCHIMERA relative that shares traits with SPAWN and exploits CVE-2025-0282; it embeds a SPAWNSLOTH variant [S4][S6].

campaigns.name: ICS compromise using CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports UNC5337 compromised ICS appliances as early as January 2024, suspected via the two CVEs disclosed 2024-01-10, using the SPAWN malware families.

campaigns.name: Mandiant 'Cutting Edge Part 4' SPAWN analysis
campaigns.summary: Mandiant published SPAWNANT, SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNSNAIL and SPAWNSLOTH analysis and, per secondary coverage, assessed with medium confidence that UNC5337 is UNC5221 (not confirmed in the post text).

campaigns.name: CVE-2025-0282 zero-day exploitation begins
campaigns.summary: Mandiant saw exploitation of the ICS stack-based buffer overflow from mid-December 2024; SPAWN deployment was attributed to UNC5337, though Mandiant did not attribute all exploitation to a single actor.

campaigns.name: Disclosure and cluster merge
campaigns.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2025-0282 and CVE-2025-0283 on 2025-01-08; Mandiant published its analysis the same day and on 2025-01-17 updated attribution to state that UNC5337 had been merged into UNC5221.

campaigns.name: CISA RESURGE analysis
campaigns.summary: CISA analyzed RESURGE, a malware variant with SPAWNCHIMERA traits exploiting CVE-2025-0282, reported by press to include a SPAWNSLOTH variant. Link to UNC5337 is not stated in the sources gathered.

diamond.adversary: Suspected China-nexus espionage cluster, now merged into UNC5221 by Mandiant [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: ICS zero-day exploitation and the SPAWN backdoor, tunneler, installer and log-tampering tools; PHASEJAM and DRYHOOK observed in CVE-2025-0282 intrusions [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised ICS VPN appliances used as footholds and tunneling points via SPAWNMOLE [S1][S2]. Actor-controlled C2 not detailed in sources gathered.
diamond.victim: Organizations running internet-facing ICS appliances; specific victims not identified in sources gathered [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Edge VPN appliances with limited host visibility; integrity checker tool can be evaded and persistence can survive upgrades [S2].

gaps: Victim sectors, regions and objectives for UNC5337 are not stated in the sources gathered [S1].
Sponsor is not named; only 'suspected China-nexus' is cited [S1][S2].
Mandiant's April 2024 post says exploitation by UNC5337 was suspected, not confirmed, for the two CVEs [S1].

Whether RESURGE/SPAWNCHIMERA is operated by UNC5337/UNC5221 is not established in the cited sources [S4][S6]. One outlet's naming of the SPAWNCHIMERA actor as UNC5325 conflicts with Mandiant naming and was not verified.
One search summary reported Microsoft attributing CVE-2025-0282 exploitation to Silk Typhoon; not verified against a primary Microsoft document and not asserted here.
CISA AR25-087A and the CISA MAR PDF appear in search results but could not be fetched (government host blocked).
No Microsoft actor name or MITRE group ID identified; MITRE ATT&CK techniques not collected here.
Press sources (TechTarget, The Hacker News) were seen only through search summaries; their pages could not be fetched.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing VPN gateways (Ivanti Connect Secure) are key terrain; compromise yields credentials, session data and an entry to Active Directory [S2]. STEP 2: The actor class exploits zero-days before disclosure and persists through upgrades and integrity checks, so patching alone does not evict it [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Template is recon of appliance version, exploitation, SELinux/syslog tampering, web shell or SPAWN backdoor, credential harvest, LDAP/SMB/RDP lateral movement, log cleaning [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued edge-appliance exploitation for persistent access and credential theft. MDCOA is use of appliance footholds to reach internal networks during a crisis. Candidate indicators: sequential requests to Host Checker version URLs, unexpected files in /tmp, SSH listener on localhost 8300, syslog forwarding stopped, fake upgrade progress, modified ICT manifest [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Track VPN appliance vulnerability and exploitation status for situational awareness, including Ivanti guidance to run the ICT and factory reset on compromise [S2]. (2) Mission assurance: assume ICT can be evaded and appliance logs may be tampered, so rely on external telemetry [S2]. (3) Credentials, API keys and certificates on affected appliances need reset after compromise [S2]. (4) Coordinate with DC3 and the DIB CS program for contractor-operated VPN gateways; attribution may lag because multiple actors exploited CVE-2025-0282 [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC5337 is a suspected China-nexus espionage actor that compromised Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances as early as Jan. 2024. UNC5337 is suspected to exploit CVE-2023-46805 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2024-21887 (command injection) for infecting Ivanti Connect Secure appliances. UNC5337 leveraged multiple custom malware families including the SPAWNSNAIL passive backdoor, SPAWNMOLE tunneler, SPAWNANT installer, and SPAWNSLOTH log tampering utility. Mandiant suspects with medium confidence that UNC5337 is UNC5221.
